pages.title: Wholesale Stainless Steel Cutlery & Flatware | Yumingxing
pages.h1: Stainless Steel Cutlery & Flatware for Wholesale and OEM
pages.description: Explore knives, forks and spoons from Yumingxing in Jieyang, China. Start with a product model and confirm the material, finish and order configuration.
pages.imageAlt: Portuguese-style stainless steel cutlery from the Yumingxing catalogue

sections.heading: Cutlery, flatware and silverware
sections.body: In North America, stainless steel cutlery is also commonly called flatware or silverware. The products on this page are stainless steel, not sterling silver. Our current five-piece collection includes a dinner knife, dinner fork, dinner spoon, salad or dessert fork and dessert spoon.

sections.heading: Choose material by component
sections.body: A material option is not a specification for every piece in a set. Agree the exact grade of the knife, fork and spoon separately. Grade descriptions alone do not establish food-contact suitability.

table.value: An option listed for the Portuguese-style collection. Ask which components and finishes are available.
Options listed for the cutlery collection; request a component-level specification.
Do not treat these descriptions as an automatic equivalence to a steel grade. Ask for the actual specification and supporting documents.

sections.heading: Finish and buying programme
sections.body: Compare actual samples under the intended lighting and handling conditions. Discuss mirror finish and the listed gold or black surface options for the current collection. Confirm the treatment, colour reference and care instructions.
bullets: Hotels and restaurants: agree set composition, handling and reorder reference.
Retail: confirm presentation, labels and retail packaging.
Wholesale: confirm quantities by item and carton.
Private label: agree logo position and packaging artwork.

sections.heading: MOQ, samples and production timing
sections.body: Request current written MOQ and production timing for the chosen model, material, quantity and packaging. Samples, logo setup, new tooling and shipping need separate confirmation. Record the approved specification before agreeing the order schedule.

faq.a: Send the component names and quantities. Confirm whether the chosen model can be quoted as individual items or a configured set.

faq.q: How do I request a sample?
faq.a: Specify the model, material, finish and delivery country. Ask for sample availability, cost and timing before payment.

pages.description: Compare the current Yumingxing cooking-tool sets. Tell us the set configuration, handle material, packaging and destination market.

sections.heading: Build the set around the tools you need
sections.body: The current catalogue covers sets with turners, ladles, skimmers and cooking spoons. The exact pieces vary by model. Specify each tool and the number of pieces rather than relying on a photograph alone.

sections.heading: Compare handle and construction options
sections.body: Choose a handle style for your channel, then confirm its exact material and attachment. A wood-pattern appearance does not by itself establish that a handle is solid wood.

sections.heading: What the quotation needs
sections.body: Send the model, tool list, quantity per set, handle and head materials, dimensions, finish, target price, destination and packaging brief. MOQ, sample availability and production lead time need confirmation for the chosen configuration.
bullets: Ask for sizes and weights of each utensil.
Specify loose packing, hanging cards or boxed sets.
Confirm logo placement, carton quantity and shipping marks.
Check care instructions against your intended usage.

pages.title: Hotel & Restaurant Cutlery Supplier in China | Yumingxing
pages.h1: Hotel & Restaurant Cutlery for Commercial Dining
pages.description: Develop a sourcing brief for dining rooms, restaurants and hospitality projects using the current Yumingxing cutlery collection.
pages.imageAlt: Portuguese-style stainless steel cutlery from the Yumingxing catalogue

sections.heading: Start with the dining setting
sections.body: Send the property type, cover count, service style and required pieces. Agree the quantity of each item, replacement stock and presentation requirements before choosing a set.

sections.heading: Evaluate handling and washing with samples
sections.body: Compare length, weight, thickness, balance, edges and tine finishing on physical samples. Share the detergents, washing conditions and intended service environment. Commercial dishwasher suitability must be checked for the actual product and finish; no unverified durability rating is implied.

sections.heading: Match an existing pattern
sections.body: Send a photo, measured dimensions or a physical sample. Ask whether an existing model is suitable or whether a new design needs feasibility and tooling review. Keep an approved reference sample for subsequent orders.

sections.heading: Plan reorders and multiple properties
sections.body: Record the model, component materials, finish reference and approved sample. Ask how future batches will be checked against that reference. If shipments involve several properties, provide item quantities and carton marks for each destination; confirm the delivery arrangement in the quotation.
bullets: Property type and cover count
Set composition and quantity per piece
Material, weight and finish expectations
Destination, target date and property-level packing labels

pages.title: OEM/ODM Cutlery & Private Label Manufacturer | Yumingxing
pages.h1: OEM/ODM Stainless Steel Cutlery for Your Brand
pages.description: Discuss a project for your brand, importing business, distribution network, retail range or hospitality group. Define the customisation before requesting a quote.
pages.imageAlt: Portuguese-style stainless steel cutlery from the Yumingxing catalogue

sections.heading: Three different project routes
sections.body: An existing model, a logo programme and a newly tooled design have different development requirements. Ask for a separate quotation and schedule for the route you need.

table.label: Existing model
table.value: Confirm the available material, finish, combination and packaging. MOQ and sample availability are model-specific.

table.label: Logo or packaging
table.value: Supply logo placement and packaging requirements. Confirm artwork compatibility, proof approval and any setup charges.

table.label: New mold or structural change
table.value: Provide a drawing or sample for feasibility review. Tooling ownership, fees, development stages and approval conditions require a written agreement.

sections.heading: Define the customisation scope
sections.body: Discuss material, size, weight, shape, finish, logo location, handle treatment, set composition and packaging. Not every option is available on every product; confirm feasibility before artwork or tooling is approved.

sections.heading: From brief to an approved order
sections.body: Brief → feasibility review → quotation → sample or tooling proposal → sample approval → production arrangements → inspection → packing and shipment. Record specification revisions so the final quotation, sample and order refer to the same version.

sections.heading: Send drawings and references
sections.body: Use the enquiry brief below to prepare model references and requirements. Attach reference images, specification sheets or drawings in your email. Ask which production artwork formats the team can accept before preparing final files.

pages.title: Cutlery Factory in Jieyang, China | Yumingxing
pages.h1: Yumingxing Cutlery Factory in Jieyang, China
pages.description: Yumingxing is based in Rongcheng, Jieyang, Guangdong, China. Contact the team to confirm the production route for your cutlery or kitchen utensil project.
pages.imageAlt: Portuguese-style stainless steel cutlery from the Yumingxing catalogue

sections.heading: Factory location and project contact
sections.body: Use the contact details on this website to arrange a discussion before travelling. Request the complete visit address, contact person and appointment details directly from the team.

sections.heading: Understand the production route
sections.body: For your specific model, ask which stages are performed in-house and which are externally supplied. A useful review covers material sourcing, forming, edge finishing, polishing, cleaning, logo application and packing.

sections.heading: What to request for a factory review
sections.body: Ask for current, model-relevant workshop photographs or a video walkthrough, equipment details for the proposed operations, and the checks used at each stage. Agree any visit or independent inspection arrangements before booking.
bullets: Material and component identification
Forming and finishing steps used for the chosen model
Sample approval and inspection records
Packing and dispatch arrangements

sections.heading: Connect the factory discussion to a real product
sections.body: Start with a catalogue model or reference sample. Record the grade, dimensions, finish and target quantity so manufacturing questions relate to your actual order rather than general capacity claims.

pages.title: Cutlery Quality Control & Compliance | Yumingxing
pages.h1: Quality Control for Stainless Steel Cutlery and Kitchenware
pages.description: Agree quality requirements for the exact product, component, material batch and destination. Request supporting documents before making compliance claims about an order.
pages.imageAlt: Portuguese-style stainless steel cutlery from the Yumingxing catalogue

sections.heading: Approve the inspection brief
sections.body: Specify dimensions, weights, edges, finish, logo, set composition and packing against the approved sample. Agree sampling methods, tolerances and acceptance criteria in writing. This page does not claim a universal AQL or certified test result.

sections.heading: Factory systems and audits
sections.body: A factory audit or management-system certificate concerns the named organisation and its stated scope. When requesting one, confirm the issuer, number, applicable entity, scope, issue date and expiry date. It does not substitute for product-specific testing.

sections.heading: Product and material documents
sections.body: A product test report concerns the identified sample and test conditions. Request the report number, date, model, material or batch reference, destination requirements and test scope. Do not assume a report for a different model or material covers your order.

sections.heading: Before you approve production
sections.body: Match the approved sample to the order specification. Confirm what records and inspection arrangements are available, who carries out any additional testing, and the timing and costs. Availability must be agreed for the project.
bullets: Do not treat a steel grade as proof of food-contact compliance.
Separate existing documentation from testing that still needs arranging.
Use only current documents within their stated scope.
Ask for model-specific care and cleaning guidance.

sections.heading: Business identity and order documents
